scope.flow: veTRUST epoch-end reward snapshot and claimRewards() distribution
scope.environment: Base L2, 2-second block times; VotingEscrow binary search with inclusive <= comparison

statements.text: Epoch n is running and Alice has TRUST locked throughout the entire epoch.
epochTimestampEnd(n) equals epochTimestampStart(n+1), the first timestamp of epoch n+1.
VotingEscrow's binary search uses inclusive <= comparison, so a checkpoint created at exactly epochTimestampEnd(n) satisfies ts <= epochTimestampEnd(n) and is included in epoch n's snapshot.
At block.timestamp == epochTimestampEnd(n), the attacker calls create_lock() with a large TRUST amount, creating a VotingEscrow checkpoint with ts = epochTimestampEnd(n).
The attacker calls claimRewards(), which queries prevEpoch = n.

totalBondedBalanceAtEpochEnd and userBondedBalanceAtEpochEnd pass _epochTimestampEnd(epoch) directly to VotingEscrow's _totalSupply and _balanceOf, so the boundary lock is counted toward epoch n's reward snapshot.
userBondedBalanceAtEpochEnd(attacker, n) is non-zero because it includes the boundary lock.
totalBondedBalanceAtEpochEnd(n) is inflated by the attacker's boundary lock.
The attacker receives a pro-rata share of epoch n's emissions as real native tokens via SatelliteEmissionsController.transfer(), extracting ~504,854 TRUST (~50.5% of epoch emissions) in the PoC.
Alice loses ~50.5% of her expected rewards because the prior-epoch denominator includes next-epoch boundary locks.

Inferred: a lock created at epochTimestampEnd(n) (the first timestamp of epoch n+1) must not be counted in epoch n's reward snapshot, so only positions active during epoch n share epoch n's emissions.
On Base L2 with 2-second block times, submitting the create_lock() transaction in the block at the boundary timestamp is feasible.

ambiguities: Report does not state whether the attacker's create_lock() call is permissionless or requires any authorization; no unauthorized-caller condition is asserted.
Report does not establish a prior transaction or pre-existing state for the attacker's TRUST balance before the boundary lock; only the boundary lock itself is described.
The ~504,854 TRUST and ~50.5% figures are PoC-specific and not tied to a stated total emission or lock amount in the fragments.
Report does not state whether claimRewards() can be called by anyone or only by the lock owner.
